bet.text: Stow the note and choose amp, trap or shooter later, because the team does not always know where a note will be needed.

demand.text: The intake was built for a large acquisition zone and a crucial role in field clean-up. For the championship the team worked on reaching the midline sooner, expecting more five- and six-note autos there.
A team strategist saw points per note as the aim and, once amplification was capped at four notes, ferrying of some kind as needed to maximize it.
On its championship alliance it played the clean-up role.

auto.text: A six-note routine, new for the championship, shoots the first two notes on the move. If the indexer beam breaks show no note, the robot slides along the midline to the next one instead of driving back to shoot.
It checks a small camera window at set spots and runs a backup path if no note is there.

cycle.text: The intake funnels the note into the indexer; a triple point sends it up the elevator for the amp or out the back to the shooter. It can amp at once or hold the note.
At East Bay, a post describes 1678 and another robot passing many notes to a shooting partner; a reply says note stealing seemed disruptive.

endgame.text: A wide pivot climber hooks the chain and pulls it down while passive rollers on the elevator roll up the stage. The amp mechanism then scores the trap.

fallback.text: The intake comes off with six bolts, so a broken one can be swapped and fixed while the robot plays.
Localization can switch between odometry only and full vision.

gave_up.text: Asked what it would change, the team mentioned under-bumper intakes but preferred over-the-bumper for the larger acquisition zone. Its first over-bumper plates bent badly, sometimes outside the frame perimeter, and it still swapped the intake about once or twice a competition.

changed.text: Alpha ran a five-note auto on day 6. Beta, with three pivoting arms, did not go well and the architecture was dropped. The interview counts three robots; the blog also names Epsilon before the competition robot.
After the first event, pocketed aluminum intake plates became polycarbonate with aluminum sides.
The printed shooter pivot gear skipped at events and gave way to a cut rack and pin pinion.

outcome.text: 56-12-1 in official play; won the Archimedes division; pick 1 of the Archimedes alliance on Einstein; ranked 10 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 55.90, Archimedes).

solves.text: Keep the center of gravity low and stop notes getting stuck under the robot

facts.text: 26 in by 26 in with MK4i swerve modules
1/16 in unpocketed belly pan, light with the most surface for electronics
A 1 in by 1 in tube between the rail and the swerve modules lowers the center of gravity and stops notes getting stuck underneath
Swerve gearing is L3, the team said in October 2024
Drive motor stator current limit
Drive motor supply current limit
Swerve current limits were lowered a bit after higher values drew too much
Pre-drilled frame tubes save time and give mounting points. One member says they cut some weight; another says holes change strength and weight little
Dented drivetrain tubes had to be swapped, most likely after high-impact collisions
1/8 in wall tube is kept for heavily loaded places such as the front and back of the drive frame

solves.text: Let the driver run into notes confidently without worrying about the bumper, over a large zone

facts.text: Polycarbonate about 6 mm thick, with aluminum on the sides
5052 aluminum, so bent parts can be bent back
Attached by six bolts for quick swaps
3D-printed blocks funnel the note toward the indexer
One motor
Full width of the robot
1/16 in aluminum on the sides strengthens the polycarbonate and protects it from damage
The aluminum also keeps the intake together if the polycarbonate breaks; in off-season practice one snapped and still ran about 5 more matches
Wrist plates went from 6061, which cracked from fatigue, to 7075, with no more issues that season
Intake plates bolt to moving wrist plates, much like 1323's 2023 robot, so a swap leaves the wrist on
A Kraken drives the pivot, with a jackshaft to keep both sides in sync, through a planetary at
The intake gears are doubled for better force distribution
The pivot is cantilevered for packaging, and because the team knew a similar pivot from its 2022 intake
Dead-axle rollers: each hub holds two bearings on a bolt through the side plate, fixed by a nut, and square nuts hold the polycarbonate tube
Hubs go onto the side plate first and then into the tube, so the side plate must flex or come off
Most roller hubs are printed in Onyx, because they take a lot of impact

cost.text: Plates bent at the first competition; after the change the team still swapped the intake about once or twice a competition
With the first, rigid plates the team had to bend the intake back after every match
The bolts for the sprocket and wrist were hard to reach

functions.name: Indexer (triple point)

solves.text: Store the note, then send it to the amp or the shooter

functions.type: roller indexer that routes the note to elevator or shooter

facts.text: Two beam breaks show that the note has entered and is held
Flips up on the shooter's dead axle to reach the electronics
In week 7 the team was swapping in a new indexer design meant to improve triple point efficiency

functions.name: Elevator and ampvator

solves.text: Lift a stowed note to the amp or trap

functions.type: single-stage elevator with amp and trap scoring

facts.text: Scores the amp and, with the climber, the trap
Two Kraken X60s at the belly pan drive the elevator
The week 7 blog calls the amp mechanism the ampvator and describes a new design to improve amp and trap ejection

solves.text: Give the note spin so its flight is stable and accurate

facts.text: Flywheels on one side only
Sides lined with Teflon
Three motors
Top and bottom flywheels
Unequal top and bottom shooter plate spacing in the public CAD is a CAD error

solves.text: Hang in the last seconds and score the trap at the same time

facts.text: Pulls the chain down while passive rollers on the elevator roll up the stage
Two Kraken X60s turn a pulley to bring the climber down

solves.text: Switch between odometry only and full vision localization, for example in auto

facts.text: Two cameras feed two coprocessors running OpenCV in a Python script to detect AprilTags
Fuses odometry error, not the full robot pose, in full-field localization

The blog reports a speaker orbit, which locks onto the speaker when shooting, during Beta bring-up in week 3, and note detection still in work on the Epsilon and competition robots late in build season
Two Arducam OV2311 cameras, each with its own Orange Pi, have crossing views so both can see the same tag
Orange Pis and Arducams gave more freedom to customize tag detection than a Limelight pipeline
An extended Kalman filter worked well; most tuning went into getting reliable vision data
The Orange Pis run through step-down converters from 12 V

solves.text: Keep all robot functions easy for one driver, with as much automation as possible

facts.text: First season for the team with one driver on one controller
LED colors show a note held, ready to shoot, ready to amp or trap, or a ferry mode
Practice on the shop field, with cycle data, guides the choice between control schemes
A two-controller setup is also available: driver moves and collects, operator scores
Requests are queued with waits for the beam breaks, so one button press runs the whole intake sequence; shooting and amp scoring use the same queue
The queue was crucial to fit every driver button on one controller

functions.name: Shooter pivot
functions.type: cut aluminum rack with a dowel-pin pinion

facts.text: The tooth profile came from 971's 2017 generator
The rack is 7075 aluminum
The pinion is dowel pins bought at length and pressed into drilled holes with retaining compound
The rack was milled in profile; a CNC router could have cut it

solves.text: Keep backlash in the shooter angle as small as possible, with several points of contact

cost.text: The first, 3D printed design skipped at the Silicon Valley and Sacramento events, and stronger prints did not fix it
The pinion sat on a long unsupported shaft, so outer supports were added to keep it in contact with the rack, which the team calls a bandaid

functions.name: Shot table
functions.type: lookup table of shooter speed and angle by distance

facts.text: Before the first event the robot was placed by hand at distance steps of
At each step the team recorded the wheel speed and angle of a shot it liked
It took many hours of moving the robot by hand, with different batches of notes

cost.text: Note wear changed the height of the shot, so the team asked event staff when worn notes would be replaced

functions.name: Note detection
functions.type: camera check that picks the auto path

facts.text: One Limelight with a Coral runs Limelight's own note model
It looks only in a heavily cropped window and only when the robot is at specific locations
Placing notes on the field and making paths on the fly was the first aim, but there was not time to finish it

solves.text: Skip a note that is not there in auto

facts.text: Testing over the 2023 season found soldered CAN far more reliable and compact than Wago or Molex connectors
Ferrules make wires in small terminals much harder to pull out

functions.name: Build sequence
functions.type: four robots in one build season

facts.text: Alpha was assembled and wired by January 11, on the 2023 Beta chassis with its intake rollers
Beta was mostly assembled on January 24 and taken apart on January 31
Epsilon, basically the competition design, was basically complete on February 11; the competition robot was mechanically assembled on February 24
The software team used Alpha through January to write autos

decisions.because: it gives a larger acquisition zone and the driver can run into notes without worrying about the bumper; Beta's under-bumper intake did not function, and with little time the team had more experience with this kind

decisions.choice: Polycarbonate intake plates with aluminum sides
decisions.because: the original plates bent a lot at the first competition and had to be bent back after every match, so the team went more flexible

decisions.choice: Stow the note and choose where it goes later
decisions.because: a partner may find a stray note for the amp or a ferried note may land where it is wanted, so the choice is worth keeping
decisions.instead_of: committing each note to one place

decisions.choice: Flywheels on one side of the shooter
decisions.because: shop testing found it gives a lot of spin, which brought accuracy

decisions.choice: Switch to a new architecture after Beta
decisions.because: Beta's under-bumper intake did not really work, its note handoff did not work at all, its trap mechanism did not reach and its weight sat to the shooter side
decisions.cost: the team says it maybe should have pivoted earlier

decisions.because: it came with a couple of weeks of knowledge, and was faster and lower risk than days or weeks of prototyping

decisions.choice: Build Alpha only for a five-note auto and driver practice
decisions.because: anything more would have slowed it; it confirmed the need for a variable angle shooter and a feed-through intake
the team found no way to package hooks on the elevator that was light, sturdy and easy to line up
decisions.instead_of: hooks on the elevator, with the intake locking it in place
